verses.text: 1:1The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
1:2Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
1:3An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
1:4Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
1:5Why should you be struck again as you add lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart in grief.
1:6From feet to head: for neither a wound nor a bruise nor an inflamed blow is there a poultice to apply, nor oil nor bandages.
1:7Your land is deserted, your cities burned by fire. Your country—foreigners consume it before you; it has been deserted, overturned by foreign peoples.
1:8Daughter Zion will be left like a tent in a vineyard, like a fruit-watcher’s shelter in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
1:9If the Lord Sabaoth had not left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.
1:10Hear the Lord’s word, rulers of Sodom! Attend to God’s law, people of Gomorrah!
1:11“What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
1:12not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
1:13you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
1:14and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
1:15Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
1:16Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
1:17Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
1:18Come, let us reason together, says the Lord. Though your sins are like purple-red, I will whiten them like snow; though they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool. [1]
1:19If you are willing and listen to Me, you will eat the land’s good things.
1:20But if you are unwilling and do not listen to Me, a sword will devour you, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.”
1:21How the faithful city Zion has become a prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness lay at rest, but now murderers!
1:22Your silver is unapproved; your retailers mix the wine with water. [1]
1:23Your rulers disobey, partners of thieves, loving gifts and pursuing repayment, not judging for orphans and not attending to widows’ judgment.
1:24Therefore thus says the Master, the Lord Sabaoth: “Woe, mighty ones of Israel! For My anger will not cease among My opponents, and I will exact judgment from My enemies.
1:25I will bring My hand against you and burn you to purity. I will destroy the disobedient, remove all lawless people from you and humble all the arrogant.
1:26I will establish your judges as before and your counselors as at the beginning. After these things you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful Metropolis Zion.
1:27For her captivity will be saved through judgment and through mercy.
1:28The lawless and sinners will be shattered together, and those abandoning the Lord will be brought to an end.
1:29For they will be ashamed of their idols, which they themselves wanted, and they were disgraced by their gardens, which they desired.
1:30For they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, like a garden that has no water.
1:31Their strength will become a stalk of tow and their works sparks of fire. The lawless and sinners will be burned together, with no one to quench.”

verses.text: 2:1The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
2:2In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

2:3and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

2:4He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war. [1]
2:5And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!
2:6For He abandoned His people, Israel’s house, because their country was filled, as from the beginning, with omens like the foreigners’ country, and many foreign children were born to them.
2:7For their country was filled with silver and gold, and their treasures had no number; the land was filled with horses, and their chariots had no number.
2:8The land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they bowed before what their fingers made.
2:9A human being bowed down, and a man was humbled; I will certainly not let them go.
2:10And now enter the rocks and hide in the earth from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
2:11For the Lord’s eyes are high, but the human being is low; humanity’s height will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
2:12For the Lord Sabaoth has a day against every insolent and arrogant person, against everyone high and elevated; they will be humbled,
2:13against every cedar of Lebanon among the high and elevated, and against every oak tree of Bashan,
2:14against every mountain and every high hill,
2:15against every high tower and every high wall,
2:16against every ship of the sea and every beautiful display of ships.
2:17Every human being will be humbled, humanity’s height will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
2:18They will hide away all the handmade things,
2:19carrying them into caves, into clefts in the rocks and into holes in the earth, from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
2:20For on that day a person will cast out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to worship, to the worthless ones and the bats,
2:21to enter holes in the solid rock and clefts in the rocks from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.

verses.text: 3:1Look now, the Master, the Lord Sabaoth, will remove from Judea and Jerusalem strong man and strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water,
3:2giant and strong man and warrior and judge and prophet and conjecturer and elder,
3:3commander of fifty and admirable counselor and wise master builder and discerning listener.
3:4I will establish young men as their rulers, and mockers will lord it over them.
3:5The people will clash, person against person and each against his neighbor. The child will collide with the elder, the dishonored with the honored.
3:6For a man will seize his brother or a member of his father’s household, saying, “You have a cloak; become our leader, and let my food be under you!”
3:7Answering on that day, he will say, “I will not be your leader, for there is neither bread nor cloak in my house. I will not be leader of this people.”
3:8For Jerusalem has been abandoned and Judea has collapsed; their tongues accompany lawlessness, disobeying what concerns the Lord, because now their glory has been humbled,
3:9and the shame of their face stood against them. They announced their sin like Sodom’s and made it manifest. Woe to their soul, for they have planned an evil plan against themselves,
3:10saying, “Let us bind the righteous person, because he is troublesome to us.” Therefore they will eat the produce of their works.
3:11Woe to the lawless! Evils according to the works of his hands will happen to him.
3:12My people, your collectors glean you, and those demanding payment lord it over you. My people, those pronouncing you blessed lead you astray and disturb the path of your feet.
3:13But now the Lord will establish Himself for judgment and will set His people before judgment.
3:14The Lord Himself will come to judgment with the people’s elders and its rulers: “Why have you burned My vineyard, while the poor person’s plunder is in your houses?
3:15Why do you wrong My people and shame the face of the poor?”
3:16Thus says the Lord: “Because Zion’s daughters were exalted and walked with high neck and glancing eyes, dragging their tunics as their feet moved and playing with their feet,
3:17God will humble Zion’s ruling daughters, and the Lord will uncover their appearance
3:18on that day, and the Lord will remove the glory of their clothing and their ornaments, hair braids, fringes and crescents,
3:19the necklace and the adornment of their face,
3:20the arrangement of glorious adornment, armlets, bracelets, a hair braid, armbands, rings and earrings,
3:21the garments bordered with purple and those purple at the center,
3:22the coverings used about the house and the transparent Laconian garments,
3:23the fine-linen, blue-purple and scarlet garments, and fine linen interwoven with gold and blue-purple, and trailing summer wraps.

3:24Instead of sweet fragrance there will be dust; instead of a belt you will gird yourself with a cord; instead of golden head adornment you will have baldness because of your deeds; instead of the tunic with purple at its center you will gird yourself with sackcloth.
3:25Your most beautiful son, whom you love, will fall by the sword, and your strong men will fall by the sword.
3:26The cases of your adornment will be humbled and mourn; you will be left alone and dashed to the ground.”

verses.text: 4:1Seven women will take hold of one man, saying, “We will eat our own bread and put on our own clothes; only let your name be called over us. Take away our disgrace!”
4:2On that day God will shine out in counsel with glory upon the earth, to exalt and glorify what remains of Israel,
4:3and those remaining in Zion and left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all those recorded for life in Jerusalem,
4:4because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

4:5He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
4:6It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.

verses.text: 5:1I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
5:2I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
5:3Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
5:4What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
5:5Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
5:6and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

5:7For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
5:8Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?
5:9For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: “If many houses come to be, great and beautiful, they will become deserted, and no one will inhabit them.
5:10For where ten pairs of oxen work, it will yield one jar, and the one sowing six artabas will yield three measures.”
5:11Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing strong drink, lingering into the evening, for wine will burn them up!
5:12For with lyre and harp, drums and flutes they drink wine, but they do not look at the Lord’s works or consider the works of His hands.
5:13Therefore My people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and there was a multitude of dead through famine and thirst for water.
5:14Hades enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without ceasing, and her glorious ones, great ones, rich ones and pestilent ones will go down.
5:15A human being will be humbled, a man dishonored, and lofty eyes humbled.
5:16The Lord Sabaoth will be exalted through judgment, and the holy God will be glorified through righteousness.
5:17Those who were plundered will be pastured like bulls, and lambs will feed upon the deserted places of those wiped out.
5:18Woe to those drawing sins as with a long cord and lawless deeds as with the strap of a heifer’s yoke,
5:19who say, “Let what He will do approach quickly, so that we may see, and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know!”
5:20Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
5:21Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
5:22Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
5:23who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!

5:24Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.

5:25The Lord Sabaoth was enraged with wrath against His people, brought His hand against them and struck them. The mountains were roused, and their carcasses became like dung in the middle of the road. In all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
5:26Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!
5:27They will not hunger or grow weary, slumber or sleep, nor loosen the belts from their waists; their sandal straps will certainly not break.
5:28Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.
5:29They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.
5:30It will cry out because of them on that day like the sound of a surging sea. They will look to the earth, and behold, harsh darkness in their perplexity.

verses.text: 6:1In the year that King Oziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up; and the house was full of His glory.
6:2And seraphim stood around Him: each one had six wings, and each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew. [1]
6:4And the lintel was lifted at the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.
6:5And I said, Woe is me, for I am pierced to the heart! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Sabaoth. [1]
6:6And one of the seraphim was sent to me, with a coal in his hand that he had taken from the altar with the tongs;
6:7and he touched my mouth and said, Behold, this has touched your lips, and will take away your iniquities and cleanse your sins.
6:8And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said, Behold, here I am; send me. [1]

6:10For the heart of this people has grown dull,
and with their ears they have heard heavily,
and they have closed their eyes;
lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears,
and understand with their heart, and turn,
and I will heal them. [1]

6:11And I said, How long, O Lord? And He said:
Until cities lie waste, without inhabitants,
and houses, without people,
and the land is left desolate.

6:12And after these things God will remove people far away;
and those who remain will multiply upon the land.

6:13And yet a tenth remains upon it;
and again it will be for plunder,
as a terebinth, and as an acorn
when it falls from its husk. [1]

verses.text: 7:1In the days of Achaz, son of Joatham, son of Oziah, king of Judea, Raasson king of Aram and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to wage war on her, but they could not besiege her.
7:2It was reported to David’s house, “Aram has come to agreement with Ephraim.” His soul and his people’s soul were distraught, as when a tree in a wood is shaken by wind.
7:3The Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Achaz, you and the remaining Jasub, your son, toward the pool of the upper road of the fuller’s field,

7:4and you will say to him, ‘Take care to be quiet, and do not fear; do not let your soul grow weak before these two smoking firebrand logs. For whenever the wrath of My anger comes, I will heal again.
7:5And the son of Aram and the son of Romelias, because they counseled an evil counsel concerning you, saying,
7:6“We will go up into Judea and, after speaking with them, turn them toward ourselves and make Tabeel’s son king over her,”
7:7thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “This counsel will certainly not endure, nor will it happen.
7:8But the head of Aram is Damascus; yet within another sixty-five years Ephraim’s kingdom will cease from being a people,
7:9and the head of Ephraim is Somoron, and the head of Somoron Romelias’s son. If you do not believe, you will certainly not understand.”’”
7:10And the Lord spoke again to Achaz, saying,
7:11Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height.
7:12And Achaz said, I will certainly not ask, nor will I put the Lord to the test at all.
7:13And he said, Hear now, O house of David: is it a small thing for you to trouble people? And how is it that you trouble the Lord?

7:14Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign:
behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son,
and you will call his name Emmanuel. [1] [2]
7:16For before the child knows good or evil, he refuses wickedness, to choose the good; and the land which you fear because of the two kings will be forsaken.
7:17But God will bring upon you, upon your people and upon your father’s house days that have not yet come since the day He removed Ephraim from Judah—the king of the Assyrians.”
7:18On that day the Lord will whistle for flies—what rules a part of Egypt’s river—and for the bee that is in the Assyrians’ country,
7:19and they will all come and rest in the country’s ravines, in holes of the rocks, in the caves, in every fissure and in every tree.
7:20On that day the Lord will shave with the great and drunken razor that is beyond the river of the king of the Assyrians—the head and the hair of the feet—and He will remove the beard.
7:21On that day a person will raise a heifer from the cattle and two sheep,
7:22and because they produce very much milk, everyone left upon the land will eat butter and honey.
7:23On that day every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels will become fallow ground and thorn.
7:24With missile and arrow they will enter there, because all the land will be fallow ground and thorn.
7:25Every mountain that is plowed will be plowed, and fear will certainly not come there; for from fallow ground and thorn it will become pasture for sheep and a trampling place for cattle.

verses.text: 8:1The Lord said to me, “Take a large new sheet and write on it with a human stylus: ‘To make plunder of spoils swiftly; for it is at hand.’”
8:2“Make reliable men witnesses for Me, Uriah and Zechariah son of Barachias.”
8:3I approached the prophetess; she became pregnant and bore a son. The Lord said to me, “Call his name Plunder-quickly, Spoil-swiftly,
8:4because before the child knows how to call father or mother, he will take Damascus’s power and Samaria’s spoils before the king of the Assyrians.”
8:5The Lord spoke to me yet again,
8:6“Because this people does not want Siloam’s water, which flows quietly, but wants to have Raasson and Romelias’s son as king over you,

8:7therefore, behold, the Lord brings up against you the river’s strong and abundant water—the king of the Assyrians and his glory. He will ascend every ravine of yours and walk over every wall of yours,
8:8and he will remove from Judea a person able to lift a head or someone strong enough to accomplish anything. His encampment will fill the breadth of your country. God is with us.”
8:9Know, nations, and be defeated! Listen, you at the farthest edge of the earth! You who have grown strong, be defeated; for even if you grow strong again, you will again be defeated.
8:10Whatever counsel you devise, the Lord will scatter; whatever word you speak will certainly not endure for you, because the Lord God is with us.
8:11Thus says the Lord: “With a strong hand they resist the course of this people’s way, saying,
8:12‘Never say hard; for everything this people says is hard.’ But do not fear its fear, and do not be troubled.
8:13Sanctify the Lord Himself, and He will be your fear.

8:14If you trust in Him, He will become a sanctuary for you, and you will not encounter Him as the stumbling of a stone or as the falling of a rock. But Jacob’s house is in a trap, and those settled in Jerusalem in a pit.
8:15Therefore many among them will be powerless, fall and be broken; people who are secure will draw near and be captured.”
8:16Then those sealing up the law so that it may not be learned will be revealed.
8:17He will say, “I will wait for God, who turned His face away from Jacob’s house, and I will put my trust in Him.”
8:18Behold, I and the children God gave me—and it will be for signs and wonders in Israel’s house, from the Lord Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion.

8:19If they say to you, “Seek those who speak from the earth and the belly-speakers, the empty-talkers who speak from the belly,” should not a nation turn to its God? Why do they seek the dead concerning the living?
8:20For He gave law for help, so that they might speak unlike this utterance, concerning which there are no gifts to give for it.
8:21A harsh famine will come upon you; when you hunger, you will be grieved and speak evil of the ruler and the cult images, and they will look up toward heaven above,
8:22and they will look down to the earth, and behold, affliction and confinement and darkness, constricted perplexity and darkness so that they cannot see,

8:23and the one in confinement will not remain perplexed for a time. “Do this first, do it quickly, country of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, way of the sea, and the rest who dwell by the sea and beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, the regions of Judea.”

verses.text:
9:2The multitude of the people whom Thou hast brought down in Thy gladness,
they will rejoice before Thee,
as people rejoice at harvest,
and as those who divide the spoils. [1]

9:5For a child was born to us,
a son also was given to us,
whose rule was laid upon his shoulder;
and his name is called Messenger of Great Counsel.
For I will bring peace upon the rulers,
peace and health to him. [1] [2] [3]

9:6Great is his rule, and his peace has no limit,
upon the throne of David and his kingdom,
to establish it and uphold it in righteousness and judgment,
from now on and for ever.
The zeal of the Lord Sabaoth will do these things.
9:7The Lord sent death against Jacob, and it came upon Israel,
9:8and all Ephraim’s people and those settled in Samaria will know, saying in insolence and a lofty heart,
9:9“Bricks have fallen, but come, let us hew stones, cut down sycamores and cedars, and build ourselves a tower.”
9:10God will dash those rising against Mount Zion upon them, and He will scatter their enemies,
9:11Syria from the sun’s rising and the Greeks from the sun’s setting, who devour Israel with their whole mouth. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
9:12The people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
9:13The Lord removed from Israel head and tail, great and small, in one day,
9:14the elder and those who show favoritism—this is the leadership—and the prophet teaching lawless things—this is the tail.
9:15Those blessing this people will lead astray, and they lead astray in order to swallow them up.

9:16Therefore God will not rejoice over their young men, and He will not pity their orphans or widows, because all are lawless and evil, and every mouth speaks unjust things. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
9:17Lawlessness will burn like fire and be consumed by fire like dry grass; it will burn in the forest’s thickets and consume together everything around the hills.
9:18Through the fury of the Lord’s anger the whole earth has been burned, and the people will be as though burned by fire. A person will not pity his brother,
9:19but will turn to the right because he will hunger, and eat from the left; a person eating the flesh of his own arm will certainly not be filled.
9:20For Manasseh will eat from Ephraim, and Ephraim from Manasseh, because together they will besiege Judah. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.

verses.text: 10:1Woe to those writing wickedness! For when they write, they write wickedness,
10:2turning aside the judgment of the poor, seizing the justice of My people’s needy, so that a widow becomes their prey and an orphan their plunder.
10:3What will they do on the day of visitation? For affliction will come to you from far away. To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory,
10:4so as not to fall into captivity? For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
10:5Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of My anger and wrath is in their hands.
10:6I will send My anger against a lawless nation, and I will command My people to take spoils and plunder, trample the cities and reduce them to dust.
10:7But he did not consider it this way and has not reckoned it this way in his soul; rather, his mind will turn aside, even to destroy not a few nations.
10:8If they say to him, “You alone are ruler,”
10:9he will say, “Did I not take the country above Babylon and Chalanneh, where the tower was built? I also took Arabia, Damascus and Samaria.
10:10As I took these in my hand, I will also take all the dominions. Wail, carved images in Jerusalem and Samaria!
10:11For as I did to Samaria and her handmade objects, so I will also do to Jerusalem and her idols.”
10:12When the Lord has finished doing all things on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will bring judgment upon the great mind—the ruler of the Assyrians—and upon the height of the glory of his eyes.
10:13For he said, “By strength I will act, and by the wisdom of understanding. I will remove nations’ boundaries, plunder their strength and shake inhabited cities.
10:14I will seize the whole inhabited world in my hand like a nest, and lift it like abandoned eggs. There is no one who will escape me or contradict me.”
10:15Will an ax be glorified without the one cutting with it, or a saw be raised without the one drawing it? Likewise, if someone lifts a rod or a piece of wood.
10:16And it will not be so; rather, the Lord Sabaoth will send dishonor against your honor, and against your glory a burning fire will burn.
10:17Israel’s light will become fire, and He will sanctify him in burning fire and consume the woodland like grass. On that day,
10:18the mountains, hills and forests will be extinguished, and it will consume from soul to flesh. The one fleeing will be like someone fleeing from a burning flame.
10:19Those left from them will be a number, and a child will write them down.
10:20On that day Israel’s remainder will no longer continue, and Jacob’s survivors will certainly no longer trust those who wronged them; rather, they will trust God, Israel’s Holy One, in truth,

24:5The earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in it, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.
24:6Therefore a curse will consume the earth, because those dwelling in it sinned. Therefore those dwelling on the earth will be poor, and few people will be left.
24:7Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.

24:10Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.
24:11Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.
24:12Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.
24:13All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations: as when someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them, even when the grape harvest has ceased.

24:15therefore the Lord’s glory will be in the sea’s islands; the Lord’s name will be glorious—O Lord, Israel’s God!
24:16From the earth’s wings we heard wonders: “Hope for the devout!” And they will say, “Woe to those who reject, those who reject the law!”
24:17Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!

24:20The earth has tilted and will be shaken like a fruit-watcher’s shelter, like someone drunk and hungover. It will fall and will never be able to rise, for lawlessness has prevailed upon it.

INTRODUCTION

Introducing Isaiah

Isaiah proclaims the holiness of God, judgement on sin and the coming salvation of Zion and the nations. With its prophecies of Immanuel and the Suffering Servant, it has been called the ‘fifth gospel’.

SETTING
Isaiah spoke to Judah and Jerusalem under the Assyrian threat; the later chapters address exiles awaiting return from Babylon.
AUTHOR
Traditionally attributed throughout to Isaiah son of Amoz. Many modern scholars assign chapters 40–66 to later prophets in his tradition.
DATE
Isaiah’s ministry c. 740–700 BC; many scholars date later sections to the 6th century BC.

Current Bespoke editorial guide

All 66 chapters, comprising 1289 existing verse units, have received the Bespoke English editorial pass: 681 revised and 608 retained. Source-specific numbering, names, repetitions and verse anchors are preserved. The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending. All English verse units were individually reviewed, and the full displayed Greek running text was read chapter by chapter with focused comparison of the recorded features. This does not constitute exhaustive critical-text verification.

The newer Bespoke PDF governs this reading edition. Saints Translation literal-smooth and all comparison/study streams remain separate and unchanged. Notes are separated from Scripture. Earlier source and wording notes are historical records and may quote superseded wording or pronouns; the dated current Bespoke notes explain this revision. The earlier editorial guide remains linked as a historical reference and does not override the newer PDF.

Greek-based verse boundaries remain intact, including the heaven-opening clause at 63:19 and the eleven verses of chapter 64. Historical lexical and comparative notes, footnote anchors, images and navigation are preserved. The chapter notes list readings that still need specialist review.
